fields.v: Each agent in its own container implements its feature per the plan, messaging the partner asynchronously at any time (max 100 actions per agent); patches merged with git merge-file (then union merge, then a fine-tuned Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B merge resolver for trivial conflicts); both features' unit tests run on the merged code. Benchmark construction: (I) repository and PR selection, (II) anchor feature from a real PR plus human-authored adjacent features (LLM-assisted ideation), tests written without coding assistants, joint gold patch; (III) containerised reproducible environments

fields.v: Benchmark CooperBench, 652 tasks. Criterion: both features' tests pass on the merged patch; no success criterion stated by the authors (Solo is the reference for the 'coordination gap'). Solo vs Coop successes (k/652; AUC Solo/Coop; retention), OpenHands v0.54: (1) GPT-5: Solo 315 (48%), Coop 183 (28%); AUC 0.506/0.325; retention 0.64. (2) Claude Sonnet 4.5: 307 (47%) vs 168 (26%); 0.469/0.283; 0.60. (3) MiniMax-M2: 236 (36%) vs 91 (14%); 0.374/0.171; 0.46. (4) Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B: 141 (22%) vs 87 (13%); 0.236/0.148; 0.63. (5) Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507: 41 (6%) vs 30 (5%); 0.106/0.072; 0.68. Coop without communication (final merge success %, with-comm in brackets): GPT-5 27.91 (27.90), Claude 27.30 (25.92), MiniMax 14.88 (13.96), Qwen3-Coder 14.72 (13.34), Qwen3-Instruct 3.37 (4.60). For each: quality verdict no criterion stated by the authors (Coop judged worse than Solo by the authors); cost not measured. Scaling (46 tasks, model not stated): 2 agents 68.6%, 3 agents 46.5%, 4 agents 30.0%

fields.v: Coop success consistently below Solo for all models ('curse of coordination'): GPT-5 and Claude Sonnet 4.5 about 25-28% Coop vs 47-48% Solo; pooled retention 0.59 (41% of Solo capability lost); gap largest at mid difficulty. Communication does not significantly change success (avg final merge effect -0.5 points) but significantly reduces naive merge conflicts; agents spend up to 20% of steps communicating. First-turn planning nearly halves conflict rate (29.4% vs 51.5%). More agents lower success (68.6% -> 46.5% -> 30.0%). Failure symptoms: work overlap 33.2%, divergent architecture 29.7%
